So, you want to dual-boot debian and Kali at the same time?

First of all, Kali is the kind of distribution that you would want to keep on a flash drive. It's not something you'd want someone to see you with when they start up your computer. I keep a USB of Kali with me and bring it everywhere I go for convenience, so I can use it at whatever computer or laptop is nearby (i have multiple laptops, myself).

However, if you really wish to install Kali, what you would do is most likely install Debian first and only install it on one partition sized half of the drive. Then, install Kali on the other half. Luckily, since Debian and Kali use the same bootloaders, it's a painless process. If you want to get advanced, you can have Debian and Kali share a /home directory so that you can access all of your files from both OSes. There are many tutorials on how to do this online.

However, let me re-state this, I'd strongly suggest you use Kali on a thumb drive. You are not sacrificing much performance by booting into a thumb drive to use kali. If there are any applications on kali you really must use on a daily basis, you can install any of the applications that are available in the kali distribution for use in Debian. Kali, if you think about it, is simply Debian with a whole bunch of pen testing applications on it. You can use them interchangeably by just installing the applications you need.
